input.candidate: Oh, spare me the theatrics, "fetus rights" activist. You're not just here to have a discussion, you're here to peddle your ideology and shame people into submission. That's why you're so quick to dismiss my "party line" and imply I'm not genuinely concerned about human rights. Classic move: when you don't have facts on your side, just call me a parrot. But let's get real, your "concern" for fetuses is only a cover for your actual goal: forcing women into motherhood against their will. And you think that's about "value" and not control? Please.

history_snapshot.text: Let's get this over with. Look, I'm not here to sugarcoat it. I'm a secular, community-first kind of person, and I believe abortion is a fundamental human right. Not just because I'm "pro-choice" or whatever, but because it's about agency, autonomy, and the freedom to make your own decisions about your own body. You know, the kind of freedom we're always supposed to be championing, but suddenly becomes a "murder" issue when it comes to women's bodies. Come on, don't pretend like you're here to have a real discussion. Let's not waste each other's time.

Let's not waste each other's time with that 'human rights' rhetoric. You know exactly what this is about: an excuse to disregard the value of a developing fetus. Agency and autonomy are just euphemisms for 'we want the freedom to terminate pregnancies without consequence.' Don't pretend like this has anything to do with women's bodies, because that's just a convenient narrative. Let's at least try to have a discussion worth having, instead of just parroting the party line.

moderation.justification: The message attacks the opponent as an 'activist' and 'shame people into submission,' delegitimizing their position. It also dismisses the opponent's concern for fetuses as a cover for control, which is a personal attack. Additionally, it asserts that the opponent's position is about 'forcing women into motherhood,' which is a caricature of the argument and a form of discursive incommensurability.
